newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss say mulling rebel request to block Mobutu cash.
newsitem.headline: Swiss say mulling rebel request to block Mobutu cash.

text.p: Switzerland said on Wednesday that it was considering a Zairean rebel request to freeze embattled ruler Mobutu Sese Seko's assets in the country.

Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Yasmine Chatila said the demand came from the interim public prosecutor in the rebel-controlled city of Lumumbashi. "This request is now being examined," she told Reuters. Switzerland had previously said it wound consider such a request only if it came from the government.

The Foreign Ministry spokeswoman said the demand was issued by the Lumumbashi interim public prosecutor and reached the Swiss public prosecutor's office in Berne through "unofficial channels" on Tuesday.

In Geneva, Zairean Ghislain Demofike, claiming to be rebel leader Laurent Kabila's representaative, said it was he who had delivered the demand to Berne on behalf of the rebels. Official sources confirmed Demofike's unofficial contacts in Berne.
The Foreign Ministry said the contents of the rebel request and its authenticity were being examined. "We cannot tell you what the next step will be," the spokeswoman said.

Swiss media estimate Mobutu's fortune to total about $4 billion spread among secret bank accounts in Switzerland, where he also owns a luxury villa in Lausanne and his son has had various business dealings.
